decisions.id: W49-3 no seat in the frame: the first seat beside it moved inward
decisions.summary: placer.place: when no candidate out to the hug lies inside the frame, the first seat beside the subject is shifted by the least that brings it inside the frame (moved_inward)
decisions.why: Round 1's NOT LEGITIMATE CONFIRMED CORRECTED: the past-the-frame seat is gone; wherever the frame can hold the caption on an axis the caption lands inside it, so 0242's 'A place that would run off the edge of the picture is never taken' and 'never left off' both hold, which is the page's purpose ('A clipped caption cannot be read'). The moved place is not one of 0242's ordered places (none of which can be taken here), so it does not narrow 'the place that covers the least'; it stays closer to the subject than a leader past the hug would, and its claim is labeled UNRESEARCHED rather than cited to 0241 as round 1 asked. Round 1 named searching past the hug as one legitimate route, not the only one; the inward move reaches the same end (never clipped where the frame can hold it).

decisions.id: W49-3a frame narrower than the caption: centered, clipped
decisions.summary: on an axis the frame is narrower than the caption, moved_inward centers it on the frame
decisions.why: The one case round 1 named as physically impossible: no place of the caption's size fits inside a frame narrower than it, so 'never clipped' cannot be honored and 'never left off' still is. Labeled in the claim (UNRESEARCHED, 'centered where the frame is narrower') and pinned by test_the_frame_is_never_left's 10 x 10 frame and the new unit test.

decisions.id: W49-4 tests restated to the page
decisions.summary: the six key-pinning tests restated; test_the_frame_is_never_left; new test_a_seat_past_the_frame_is_moved_inward_until_it_fits
decisions.why: Round 1's exception CONFIRMED CORRECTED: test_the_frame_is_never_left keeps its meaning (a 510-wide frame takes 'left', not a seat leaving it; only the 10 x 10 impossible frame reaches the fallback, now centered), and the new test pins both branches of moved_inward. decisions.id: W50-2 row 513: the sluice's box from its span, drawn true
decisions.summary: matrix box (span, 8.4); default frame 20 ft at the map's scale with no 10.8 px floor; 0179 section 12 reworded to timbers and drum larger than life, span true; a dike gate bank to bank on a wider channel, posts 2 ft past each bank (GUESS)
decisions.why: Row 76's fix (size from the span, 16-24 ft, bank to bank on a wider channel). The 0179 rewording is not research bent to the code: section 12 was a CONVENTION with no source, and it contradicted the page's own section 13 (16-24 ft span); keeping the convention for timbers and drum, and drawing the span true, follows section 13 and the standing no-inflation rule for to-scale maps. The 2 ft past each bank is a labeled GUESS inside 0179's 'bank to bank'. Kuwabata's channels (5 ft) leave every gate at 20 ft, the same as before at its scale: only the two records gained span 20 (pool diff checked).

decisions.id: W50-3 rows 523-525: a join rules a seat out; the widest seat left takes the crossing

decisions.why: 0084's drawing page says both, word for word: 'the joins of ditches rule a seat out and the span stays about 8 ft' and 'Where no wide spot is free, a crossing takes the widest spot left ... rather than left off'. The ditch still qualifies by its widest point (worth_planking, page section 'A ditch is judged by its widest point'), so no crossing is added on water the page says is stepped across. decisions.id: W50-5 row 527: work yards off only where no grain is grown
decisions.summary: grows_grain: off only on a dike-pond hamlet whose leftover parcels are ponds
decisions.why: Row 108's fix ('key off on no grain crop, not on no rice'); 0037: every rice and dry-field farm keeps a yard. Checked against the GM's 2026-08-28 ruling (feature 150 T41): its words are 'no threshing yards on a no-rice hamlet', its stated basis 'rice is what a threshing floor is for'; a dike-pond hamlet whose leftover parcels stand in rice is not a no-rice hamlet, so the change follows both the research and the ruling's own words. Note for the GM, not a block: the ruling was carried out on the whole archetype when the leftover form could already be standing rice, so a future rolled dike-pond hamlet with rice leftovers now draws yards where 2026-08-28's build drew none. No kept map moves (Kuwabata's leftover is pond).
